30961-the-rushton-boys-at-rally-hall-or-.title: Great Days in School and Out
30961-the-rushton-boys-at-rally-hall-or-.creator: Spencer Davenport
30961-the-rushton-boys-at-rally-hall-or-.description: A book by Spencer Davenport. Fred Rushton, who had hit the ball, was streaking it for second, and Jim, forgetting his injured hand, picked up the ball and threw it in. Fred saw that it was going to be a tight squeeze and made a slide for the base. The ball got there at almost the same time, and for a moment there was a flying tangle of arms and legs.

46331-merrie-england-in-the-olden-time-v.description: A book by George Daniel. |Youth is the season of ingenuousness and enjoyment, when we desire to please, and blush not to own ourselves pleased. At that happy period there is no affectation of wisdom; we look only to the bright and beautiful: we inquire not whether it be an illusion; it is sufficient that fairy land, with its flowers of every hue, is the path on which we tread.

arxiv-2006-06122.title: DNS Tunneling: A Deep Learning based Lexicographical Detection Approach
arxiv-2006-06122.creator: Franco Palau, Carlos Catania, Jorge Guerra, Sebastian Garcia, Maria Rigaki
arxiv-2006-06122.description: Abstract Domain Name Service is a trusted protocol made for name resolution, but during past years some approaches have been developed to use it for data transfer. DNS Tunneling is a method where data is encoded inside DNS queries, allowing information exchange through the DNS.

arxiv-2104-08440.title: Learning on a Budget via Teacher Imitation
arxiv-2104-08440.creator: Ercüment İlhan, Jeremy Gow and Diego Perez-Liebana
arxiv-2104-08440.description: Abstract Deep Reinforcement Learning (RL) techniques can benefit greatly from leveraging prior experience, which can be either self-generated or acquired from other entities. Action advising is a framework that provides a flexible way to transfer such knowledge in the form of actions between teacher-student peers.

arxiv-2110-14110.title: Mining frequency-based sequential trajectory co-clusters Journal: Journal of L a T e X Templates
arxiv-2110-14110.creator: Yuri Santos, Jônata Tyska, Vania Bogorny
arxiv-2110-14110.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Yuri Santos, Jônata Tyska, Vania Bogorny. Co-clustering is a specific type of clustering that addresses the problem of finding groups of objects without necessarily considering all attributes. This technique has shown to have more consistent results in high-dimensional sparse data than traditional clustering.

arxiv-2210-04039.title: Multi-mode Jaynes-Cummings model results for the collapse and the revival of the quantum Rabi oscillations in a lossy resonant cavity
arxiv-2210-04039.creator: Najirul Islam, Shyamal Biswas
arxiv-2210-04039.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Najirul Islam, Shyamal Biswas. We have numerically obtained theoretical results for the collapse and the revival of the quantum Rabi oscillations for low average number of coherent photons injected on a two-level system in a lossy resonant cavity. We have adopted the multimode Jaynes-Cummings model for the same and especially treated the “Ohmic” loss to the walls of the cavity, the leakage from the cavity, and the loss due to the spontaneous emission through the open surface of the cavity.

The views and conclusions contained herein are those of t
arxiv-2212-02376.creator: Peiwen Qiu Yining Li Zhuqing Liu Prashant Khanduri Jia Liu, Ness B. Shroff Elizabeth Serena Bentley Kurt Turck
arxiv-2212-02376.description: Abstract Decentralized bilevel optimization has received increasing attention recently due to its foundational role in many emerging multi-agent learning paradigms (e.g., multi-agent meta-learning and multi-agent reinforcement learning) over peer-to-peer edge networks. However, to work with the limited computation and communication capabilities of edge networks, a major challenge in developing decentralized bilevel optimization techniques is to lower sample and communication complexities.

arxiv-2305-00836.title: Siegel modular forms with extra twists Thanks: The first named author was partially supported by the SERB grant MTR/2017/000357 and CRG/2020/000223. We thank Professor Abhishek Saha for fruitful email correspondence in the initial stage of the project.
arxiv-2305-00836.creator: Debargha Banerjee and Ronit Debnath
arxiv-2305-00836.description: Abstract . In this paper, we study Siegel modular forms with extra twists. We provide conditions on the level and genus of the forms that is necessary for the existence of extra twists for Siegel modular forms. We also give explicit examples of Siegel modular forms with extra twists that are different from the complex conjugation.

arxiv-2310-01433.title: AI-Aristotle: A Physics-Informed framework for Systems Biology Gray-Box Identification Journal: arXiv.org
arxiv-2310-01433.creator: Nazanin Ahmadi Daryakenari, Mario De Florio, Khemraj Shukla, George Em Karniadakis
arxiv-2310-01433.description: Abstract Discovering mathematical equations that govern physical and biological systems from observed data is a fundamental challenge in scientific research. We present a new physics-informed framework for parameter estimation and missing physics identification (gray-box) in the field of Systems Biology.

arxiv-2407-01070.title: Dark Photon Dark Matter in Quantum Electromagnetodynamics and Detection at Haloscope Experiments
arxiv-2407-01070.creator: Chang-Jie Dai, Tong Li, Rui-Jia Zhang
arxiv-2407-01070.description: Abstract The ultralight dark photon is one of intriguing dark matter candidates. The interaction between the visible photon and dark photon is introduced by the gauge kinetic mixing between the field strength tensors of the Abelian gauge groups in the Standard Model and dark sector.

arxiv-2601-13532.title: An upper limit on cosmological chiral gravitational wave background
arxiv-2601-13532.creator: Mohammad Ali Gorji, Ashu Kushwaha, Teruaki Suyama
arxiv-2601-13532.description: Abstract Within the standard framework in which electroweak sphaleron processes relate lepton and baryon number, we derive an upper limit on the amplitude of a chiral gravitational wave background produced prior to the electroweak epoch. This bound is independent of the production time of chiral GWs for superhorizon modes, while it becomes sensitive to the production time for subhorizon modes.

arxiv-2602-04395.title: Mechanisms of localization in a finite harmonically confined optical superlattice
arxiv-2602-04395.creator: A. Katsaris †, I. A. Englezos †, C. Weitenberg, F. K. Diakonos, P. Schmelcher
arxiv-2602-04395.description: Abstract We investigate the impact of harmonic confinement in a finite optical superlattice and reveal the different mechanisms that can lead to the emergence of localized states. The optical superlattice, with odd or even number of unit cells, can exhibit either a trivial or a non-trivial underlying topology, characterized by the corresponding Zak phase.

pmc-12617629.title: Persistent memory in network topologies following temporary stimuli
pmc-12617629.creator: Federico Sevlever, Ariel Waisman, Santiago Miriuka, Alejandra C Ventura
pmc-12617629.description: SummaryMolecular memory in signaling and gene regulatory networks shapes how cells respond to transient inputs. Here, we present a mathematical framework to quantify memory as changes in system state after temporary stimulation. Using computational models, we show that circuits with positive feedback loops, particularly those enabling bistability, sustain long-term memory, while certain negative feedbacks can erase it.

pmc-13025393.title: Molecular Pathology, Artificial Intelligence, and New Technologies in Hematologic Diagnostics: Translational Opportunities and Practical Considerations
pmc-13025393.creator: Fnu Alnoor, Shuvam Mukherjee, Madhu P. Menon, David Ng, Peng Li, Robert S. Ohgami
pmc-13025393.description: Background and Objectives: Diagnostics for hematologic diseases rely on integrated assessment of clinical manifestation, morphology, flow cytometry, and molecular testing. Current classification systems, including the WHO HAEM5 and the International Consensus Classification, highlight the central role of genomics in defining disease entities and risk. Simultaneously, laboratories face growing case complexity and staffing challenges.

pmc-13282349.title: Segmentation of blush size guides embolic endpoints in genicular artery embolization
pmc-13282349.creator: Arian Taheri Amin, Eva Kemmer, Ann-Joelle Hübner, Lena Marie Wilms, Paula Krüselmann, Farid Ziayee, Christian Rubbert, Kai Jannusch, Peter Minko
pmc-13282349.description: ObjectiveTo identify a quantitative surrogate parameter for the embolic endpoint in genicular artery embolization (GAE).Materials and methodsDigital subtraction angiography (DSA) images were fused and converted into color maps. Using segmentation software, blush size was measured before and after embolization, and blush reduction ratio (BRR) was calculated.

pmc-13331252.title: Efficacy of a Cognitive Behavioral Therapy–Based Online Self-Help Group for Depression and Suicide Ideation: Randomized Controlled Trial
pmc-13331252.creator: Minkyung Yim, Haeun Kim, Soo-Eun Lee, Eunjin Jo, Ji-Won Hur, Lorraine Buis
pmc-13331252.description: BackgroundDespite the high prevalence of depressive disorders, access to effective treatment remains limited due to financial, geographic, and social barriers. Online self-help groups offer a promising and scalable form of peer-based support beyond traditional clinical settings. Integrating cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) techniques such as cognitive restructuring and behavioral activation into self-help groups may enhance their effectiveness.

pmc-13395867.title: Frequency-dependent coupling in response to oscillatory inputs in minimal networks of electrically coupled nodes: Gap junction networks and spatially extended neurons
pmc-13395867.creator: Andrea Bel, Ulises Chialva, Horacio G Rotstein
pmc-13395867.description: In electrically coupled networks, the coupling coefficient (CC) quantifies the strength of the connectivity between pairs of nodes. The CC is typically measured by computing the relative stationary responses to constant inputs of the indirectly activated (post-J) and the directly activated (pre-J) nodes.

pmc-13429511.title: Editorial: Molecular characterization of thyroid lesions in the era of “next generation” techniques, volume III
pmc-13429511.creator: Umberto Malapelle, Dario de Biase
pmc-13429511.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). s; today, the molecular profile represents an essential component of integrated diagnostics and precision medicine. This Research Topic collects nine contributions that, taken together, clearly outline the transition from a descriptive view of thyroid disease to a multilevel interpretative model, in which driver mutations, transcriptomic profiles, serological biomarkers, predictive algorithms, and new sequencing platforms converge towards a more accurate stratification of biological and clinical risk.

pmc-13474188.title: Geometry‐Encoded Actuation as a Structural Interaction Layer in Origami Robots
pmc-13474188.creator: Jianshu Zhou, Yitong Li, Junda Huang, Ian Zhang, Haoran Liu, Boyuan Liang, Yiyuan Zhang, Xiaohui Xiao, Qiguang He
pmc-13474188.description: Physical interaction in robotics predominantly relies on sensing, computation, and feedback control, resulting in increasing system complexity. Here, we introduce geometry‐encoded actuation (GEA), a design framework that exploits multistable origami geometries as programmable physical interaction layers to mechanically encode environmental stimuli into autonomous structural responses.

pmc-13479262.title: Prehospital 12-lead ECG and outcomes in acute coronary syndrome
pmc-13479262.creator: Timothy John Driscoll, Sarah Black, Glenn Davies, Chris P Gale, Lucia Gavalova, Mary Halter, Chelsey Hughes, Scott Munro, Nigel Rees, Andy Rosser, Helen Snooks, Alan Watkins, Clive Weston, Tom Quinn
pmc-13479262.description: Importance/backgroundThe 12-lead ECG is recommended in clinical guidelines for prehospital assessment of patients with suspected acute coronary syndrome (ACS) presenting to Emergency Medical Services (EMS).ObjectivesTo determine prehospital ECG (PHECG) utilisation since UK national rollout of primary percutaneous coronary intervention, and whether this is associated with clinical outcomes in patients with ACS.

pmc-13653295.title: Towards Optimized Awake Bruxism Metrics: Empirical Definition of Minimal Ecological Momentary Assessment Requirements
pmc-13653295.creator: Alona Emodi‐Perlman, Lihi Keren, Anna‐Yael Czygrinow, Khalil Masarwe, Noa Ventura, Ilana Eli
pmc-13653295.description: BackgroundEcological Momentary Assessment (EMA) is increasingly used to assess awake bruxism (AB) in real time. However, current protocols typically require 7 days of monitoring and high daily response rates, potentially limiting compliance.ObjectivesTo empirically establish the shortest monitoring duration and daily response threshold that still yield reliable estimates of AB behaviours through smartphone‐based EMA.
